about: The moments library (Erick 2026-10-17). Each moment is solved for the shot's own day by moments.js, from the daemon (CELESTIAL_RENDER_SKY) and the measured 2500 BC skyline seen from the circle centre (w6/hz360_dtm_stage2.tsv, eye 1.6 m). A shot's light may say "from": "@sunrise_gleam-2m", "to": "@sunrise_whole+3m", "held": "@sunset_half". 'best_takes' points into cameras.json.

sunrise_gleam.what: first light: the Sun's upper limb clears the real skyline
sunrise_gleam.lasts: an instant; the disc takes ~2.7 min to clear in summer

sunrise_half.what: half the disc above the skyline (the bearing quoted for alignments)

sunrise_whole.what: the whole disc clear of the skyline

sunset_sits.what: the lower limb touches the skyline

sunset_half.what: half-set: the disc centre on the skyline (the bearing quoted for alignments)

sunset_gone.what: last gleam: the upper limb drops below the skyline

golden_morning_end.what: the Sun reaches 6° (end of the low warm light)

golden_evening_start.what: the Sun drops to 6° (long shadows, warm light)

low_sun_3_morning.what: the Sun at 3° in the morning — the contrast height (same shadows length on every day)

low_sun_3_evening.what: the Sun at 3° in the evening — the contrast height

civil_dawn.what: civil dawn (Sun −6°): the sky glows, stones in silhouette

civil_dusk.what: civil dusk (Sun −6°): afterglow, first bright stars

nautical_dusk.what: nautical dusk (Sun −12°): the sky dark enough for the constellations

solar_noon.what: the Sun at its highest (shortest shadows, the meridian)

moonrise_upper.what: the Moon's upper limb clears the skyline

moonset_upper.what: the Moon's last gleam over the skyline
